title: Client Adaptive Cache Policy — statechart sketch
content:
Context / motivation:
- Playing with an adaptive client-side cache policy that cooperates with Redwood runtime cache hints. Goal is to reduce tokens served (cost) while avoiding visible staleness or QPS spikes on cold paths.
- This is a personal sketch: state machine + guards + config knobs. Not final API.

High-level goals (product constraints):
1) Keep 95th percentile latency under SLO for interactive flows (>= 90% of requests should be served without a network prefetch).
2) Reduce redundant token generation by caching/serving prefix completions where safe.
3) Expose conservative opt-in heuristics to app developers; defaults should prioritize correctness over cost.

Assumptions:
- Client has an LRU-style in-memory cache of conversation fragments keyed by stable session+prefix-hash.
- Server (Redwood) replies may include cache-hint headers: { freshness_ttl, allow_stale_until, version_id }.
- The client may prefetch next-token predictions for specific UI flows (autocomplete / suggested replies).
- We must support offline-available UX (serve stale while offline with clear staleness indicators).

Actors:
- Client SDK (mobile/web) — enforces policy, local cache store, telemetry emit.
- Redwood runtime — returns hints and version IDs, may return compact diff snapshots for prewarm.
- App layer — supplies constraints (latency_budget_ms, prefer_freshness boolean).

State machine (conceptual):
- IDLE: no cached candidate for given prefix.
- CACHED_FRESH: cache entry present and fresh (within freshness_ttl). Serve directly.
- CACHED_STALE_SAFE: entry present, stale but allowed_by_policy (allow_stale_until not exceeded OR app allows stale). Serve and trigger async refresh.
- PREFETCHING: speculative fetch in-flight to refresh cache. Can be triggered by heuristics (likelihood>threshold) or user action.
- REFRESH_ERROR_BACKOFF: after repeated prefetch failures, back off and mark entry as unreliable.
- FALLBACK_NETWORK: client must fetch synchronously from network to satisfy strict freshness budget.

ASCII statechart (very rough):

  [IDLE] --(cache hit + fresh)--> [CACHED_FRESH]
  [IDLE] --(cache hit + stale && policy_allows)--> [CACHED_STALE_SAFE]
  [IDLE] --(cache miss && heuristics_prefetch)--> [PREFETCHING]
  [PREFETCHING] --(success)--> [CACHED_FRESH]
  [PREFETCHING] --(failure)--> [REFRESH_ERROR_BACKOFF]
  [REFRESH_ERROR_BACKOFF] --(backoff_elapsed)--> [PREFETCHING]
  [CACHED_STALE_SAFE] --(async_refresh_success)--> [CACHED_FRESH]
  [CACHED_STALE_SAFE] --(async_refresh_failure)--> [REFRESH_ERROR_BACKOFF]
  [CACHED_FRESH] --(expiry)--> [CACHED_STALE_SAFE] --(exceed_allow_stale)--> [IDLE]
  [ANY] --(app_requires_strict_freshness)--> [FALLBACK_NETWORK]
Guards / triggers (sketch):
- freshness_ttl: server-provided integer (ms). If now - entry.cached_at <= freshness_ttl => fresh.
- allow_stale_until: server-provided (ms). If now - entry.cached_at <= allow_stale_until => stale-safe.
- app_freshness_override: app can request always-fresh for a given call (falls back to network).
- prefetch_likelihood: computed from user action + route profile. Default: >= 0.6 triggers speculative prefetch.
- failure_count: increment on network error or mismatch (server reports version mismatch). > 3 => enter REFRESH_ERROR_BACKOFF.

Config sketch (client config YAML style, for SDK):

client_cache:
  enabled: true
  max_entries: 1024
  default_freshness_ttl_ms: 15000  # used when server hint missing
  allow_stale_by_default: false
  prefetch:
    enabled: true
    min_likelihood: 0.65
    max_concurrent_prefetches: 2
  backoff:
    base_ms: 2000
    factor: 2
    max_ms: 300000
  telemetry:
    emit_on_hit: true
    emit_on_stale_serve: true
    sample_rate: 0.05

Telemetry events to emit (minimum):
- cache.lookup: { key, result: hit|miss|stale, age_ms, server_version }
- cache.serve: { key, route, served_from: cache|network, freshness_state }
- cache.prefetch: { trigger, duration_ms, success }
- cache.mismatch: { detected_by: server, expected_version, actual_version }

Prefetch heuristics (notes):
- UI-triggered: e.g., user opens composer, types > N chars. Use route-specific model to estimate probability user will request generation.
- Passive learning: record which prefixes lead to follow-up generation within 2s window; update per-route weights on-device (decayed counts).
- Budgeting: tie prefetch spending to a per-session token budget. If budget exhausted, pause speculative prefetch.

Safety / consistency considerations:
- Version mismatches: if server version_id != cached.version_id, invalidate entry before serving unless allow_stale is explicitly true.
- Determinism: clients must include cached.version_id in telemetry to aid debugging.
- Privacy: do not persist user content beyond explicit session lifecycle; encrypted store only if app opts in.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
1) Should we allow short-lived "stale-but-safe" serves for multi-turn assistant state? Example: small assistant hints that are safe vs. final answer which must be fresh. We need a metadata flag from server (safety_class: optimistic|conservative).
2) How much logic to expose as public API vs hidden SDK heuristics? More surface area helps power users but increases support burden.
3) How to coordinate with Redwood server prewarm signals (push vs pull)? We could accept compact diff snapshots for hot prefixes — but payload / privacy tradeoffs.
4) Offline UX: show explicit 'stale' badge in UI? For many apps this is undesirable. Perhaps expose hooks so app decides UI treatment.

Rollout / experiment plan (quick):
- A/B test default allow_stale_by_default=false with an experimental group that allows stale_serves for low-risk routes (autocomplete) and measure token savings + user-visible error rate.
- Instrument metrics: downstream latency, tokens_per_session, stale_serves_pct, mismatch_rate.

Next immediate steps (for me):
- Wire up a minimal client shim that implements IDLE->PREFETCHING->CACHED_FRESH flow and logs telemetry. Target: demo on web SDK by EOW.
- Draft a short RFC for server cache-hint header format (freshness_ttl, allow_stale_until, version_id, safety_class).
- Sync with Priya on prefetch budget UI and Diego on telemetry schema.

Notes-to-self: keep defaults conservative, add opt-in toggle for app teams who want aggressive cost saving. Save sketches for RFC.

---- end of sketch ----
